skills.name: Man in the equatorial zone: problems and solutions

vars.p: a farmer who cleared forest three years ago

worked_example.problem: Why do the crops of {p} grow worse each year?
steps: Once the forest is cleared, heavy rain falls directly on the soil.
It washes the nutrients down out of reach (leaching) and erodes the topsoil, so the soil becomes poor.
worked_example.answer: Leaching and erosion make the soil poor after the forest is cleared.

cards.idea: Heavy rain leaches nutrients from cleared soils and causes erosion.
example: Soils become poor after a few years of farming.

cards.idea: Diseases such as malaria and sleeping sickness are common in the hot, wet forest.
example: Mosquitoes and tsetse flies thrive there.

cards.idea: Solutions: roads, fertilisers, replanting, parks and disease control.

pick.r: rain water washing nutrients down out of the soil
pick.y: Heavy rain carries nutrients down beyond the roots.

pick.q: Why does food rot quickly in the equatorial zone?
pick.r: The high heat and humidity help moulds and bacteria grow.
pick.y: Warm, damp conditions speed up decay.
